FRONT 1 - sobelow carryover, land it. First read of b48fb6c1 is encouraging: the reconcile script does clear-skip THEN mark-skip-all, guards the CI toolchain (1.18.1/OTP27) and refuses on a dev box, backs up + restores .sobelow-skips byte-for-byte (never commits), and uploads the regenerated baseline+diff as a human-review artifact; the fresh-finding guard plants a non-controller String.to_atom and asserts exit 1 + a DOS.StringToAtom hit - exactly the D41 shape. Harden only if a gap is proven. Closing the task is a foreign-claim mechanics puzzle - the lander lands the BRANCH; the lead closes the ledger without stomping the live claim.

FRONT 2 - kill the ledger off-by-one at the tool, not by hand. Seam: api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex (+ criteria.ex, the /v1 close route, internal/cli close verb). Wave-7 review log names the scar: builders pass a 1-based --criterion index into a 0-based tool, so the MERGE criterion reads falsely met=true and the first real criterion falsely unmet - and separately the final LEAD-CLOSED-on-merge criterion sits met=false until a human patches it. The fix must make close auto-stamp the final merge-gated criterion met=true, writing close evidence (worker + epoch + merge commit/PR). Crux for survey: how is the final merge-gated criterion IDENTIFIED (last entry? a marker string like LEAD-CLOSED / merged? a flag on the criterion)? The fix must be CONSERVATIVE - only stamp a criterion unambiguously the merge gate, never fabricate met=true on a non-gate criterion. Prefer an explicit close-time flag over a fragile heuristic if identification is ambiguous. Fail-before: a close today leaves the final criterion met=false; after the fix it is met=true with evidence. Watch OpenAPI: if the close route request/response shape changes, docs/openapi.json needs a CI-artifact regen (local regen OOMs).

FRONT 2 seam + guardrail: auto-stamping inside the builder's own bp task close fires BEFORE merge and would recreate Mode-A's premature-true bug — the fix MUST be a lead/merge-time seam. Use an EXPLICIT flag, never a text heuristic: criterion TEXT is work-digest-defining, so matching on it risks tripping the claim fence. content.value: req-default-timeout: PREMISE REFUTED. Req 0.5.17 / Finch 0.21.0 supply a bounded 15_000ms receive_timeout default; a live probe (Req.get, no receive_timeout, against a 25s slow raw-TCP server) returned {:error, %Req.TransportError{reason: :timeout}} at 15164 ms — bounded, not a hang. SSO omitting the option drops from an availability scar to a low-severity consistency nit (backlog). Coverage: every OTHER outbound Req module sets receive_timeout explicitly (self_update 10s, webhooks 10s, github/indx/bokbasen 30s, titles 15s); no app-level default override exists.

Cdn.publish blocks the caller for the full CDN round-trip inline in both upload sites (media/processing.ex:38 and media_processing_controller.ex:25, before json(conn,...)). Proof: slow-CDN Bypass -> Cdn.publish wall-clock 916/1103ms vs 0-7ms noop control. The wish

Close the CI-hardening backlog AND run one fresh Phoenix-mastery audit pass. THREE fronts, all opus.

(1) LAND the sobelow reconcile branch (b48fb6c1): reconcile-not-append baseline regen + fresh-finding guard, run on the CI toolchain (1.18.1/OTP27), never a dev-box commit. (2) FIX THE RECURRING LEDGER TOOLING BUG at the tool level: every wave, builders leave the final LEAD-CLOSED-on-merge criterion met=false and a reviewer/steward hand-patches it. Also mergeable if it fits: task-felix-migration-ddl-audit-deadlock (D35) - its audit-dispatch 40P01 sync toggle is still UNMERGED on origin/main; land it (merge/verify, stack-attribute any 40P01).

Direction (tentative - Decide finalizes after two explore rounds)

Finish over net-new. Three disjoint, parallelizable opus worktrees, each with a fail-before proof, gated CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test, branched from ORIGIN/main (local checkout diverged with unrelated omx commits - never build from it).

FRONT 1 - sobelow carryover, land it. First read of b48fb6c1 is encouraging: the reconcile script does clear-skip THEN mark-skip-all, guards the CI toolchain (1.18.1/OTP27) and refuses on a dev box, backs up + restores .sobelow-skips byte-for-byte (never commits), and uploads the regenerated baseline+diff as a human-review artifact; the fresh-finding guard plants a non-controller String.to_atom and asserts exit 1 + a DOS.StringToAtom hit - exactly the D41 shape. FRONT 2 - kill the ledger off-by-one at the tool, not by hand. Seam: api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex (+ criteria.ex, the /v1 close route, internal/cli close verb). Wave-7 review log names the scar: builders pass a 1-based --criterion index into a 0-based tool, so the MERGE criterion reads falsely met=true and the first real criterion falsely unmet - and separately the final LEAD-CLOSED-on-merge criterion sits met=false until a human patches it. Crux for survey: how is the final merge-gated criterion IDENTIFIED (last entry? a marker string like LEAD-CLOSED / merged? a flag on the criterion)? The fix must be CONSERVATIVE - only stamp a criterion unambiguously the merge gate, never fabricate met=true on a non-gate criterion. Prefer an explicit close-time flag over a fragile heuristic if identification is ambiguous. Fail-before: a close today leaves the final criterion met=false; after the fix it is met=true with evidence. Watch OpenAPI: if the close route request/response shape changes, docs/openapi.json needs a CI-artifact regen (local regen OOMs).

The 12 domains were framework-structural; Part XI got a verdict-table Paper (Interop live, Mailers/i18n/Assets/GraphQL mostly n-a/already-good). The ripest uncovered scar-class is the OUTBOUND I/O boundary that is NOT System.cmd/Port (the interop sweep already bounded those): outbound HTTP - webhook dispatch, CDN purge/invalidate, self-update fetches, any Finch/Req/HTTPoison/:httpc call - where a missing timeout, retry storm, or connection-pool exhaustion is a real availability scar. What is established

No is_merge_gate field exists anywhere in the schema — identification today is pure convention (LAST array entry + literal 'MERGE GATE' substring, 8/8 sampled). Use an EXPLICIT flag, never a text heuristic: criterion TEXT is work-digest-defining, so matching on it risks tripping the claim fence. FRONT 3 target: outbound-HTTP is the freshest ground (System.cmd/Port already swept; mailer, webhook dispatcher, ETS caches and JSON/atom paths all independently confirmed already-hardened). Two candidate findings. (a) sso/oidc/http.ex + sso/social/http.ex are the ONLY two outbound-HTTP modules in api/lib with NO explicit receive_timeout/retry, sitting on the user-facing login path — but whether this is a real unbounded-hang or a style nit hinges on Req 0.5.17's DEFAULT receive_timeout when unset (undetermined this pass). Shared Finch default pool (only Sync.Finch is dedicated) is real but architecturally larger — file as a child task, do not build this wave.

The fix lives on local branch loop-epic/migration-ddl-deadlock-sync-in-test-audi-2 (commit 60966bdc, 4 files: config.exs, test.exs, dispatcher.ex, audit_dispatch_test.exs).
